verdict.rationale: The evidence shows vendor-specific acceleration only for Apple silicon (MetalRT, which uses Metal 3.1 GPU features and requires M3 or later) and Qualcomm Hexagon NPUs. There is also a general claim of a kernel pipeline that validates kernels against the target silicon. Nothing documents NVIDIA or AMD GPU support, so the multi-vendor GPU core of the story is mostly unevidenced. Missing for 10: NVIDIA (CUDA) GPU kernels, AMD (ROCm) GPU kernels, documented GPU vendor coverage matrix, and Apple M1/M2 GPU acceleration (currently falls back to llama.cpp).

support.subject: As a power-user, I can run models on NVIDIA, AMD, or other GPU vendors using vendor-specific acceleration kernels

citations.quote: MetalRT uses Metal 3.1 GPU features available on M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, M4, and later chips.
An agentic kernel pipeline generates, compiles, and **validates every kernel against the silicon it runs on**.
Accelerated by whatever silicon the device has.
